14/G.goal: Explain the main hardware elements of virtual reality systems, from non-hand input to processing and output devices, and how each supports immersion and interaction.
14/G.achieves: Provides the foundational VR hardware knowledge needed to understand later XR topics and to evaluate hardware choices for immersive systems.

14/O1.goal: Explain how virtual reality systems capture user input without hand controllers, including full-body tracking and sound-based tracking methods.
14/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a basis for identifying non-hand input hardware and understanding how movement and sound are captured in VR applications.

14/O2.goal: Describe the processing component of virtual reality systems and how the GPU, CPU, and RAM support rendering and system performance.
14/O2.achieves: Lets the learner understand the computational requirements of VR and the factors that matter when choosing a processing platform or middleware.

14/O3.goal: Describe the main output devices of virtual reality systems and how visual displays and non-visual sensory devices support immersion.
14/O3.achieves: Enables the learner to evaluate how different displays and sensory feedback technologies affect presence, usability, and the overall XR experience.
